title: Ex 2.6 #14 · P ∧ (Q ∨ ∼Q) vs (∼P) ⇒ (Q ∧ ∼Q)
prompt: Are $P \wedge (Q \vee \sim Q)$ and $(\sim P) \Rightarrow (Q \wedge \sim Q)$ logically equivalent? Decide, and back up your answer with a truth table, a chain of known equivalences, or a row where the two statements differ.
answer_format: equivalent or not equivalent. Steps are optional: truth-table columns, rewrite steps, or a row like P = T, Q = F where the two statements differ.
hints: Q ∨ ∼Q is always true and Q ∧ ∼Q is always false. Simplify each statement with that.
An implication with an always-false conclusion is true exactly when its hypothesis is false.
solution: $Q \vee \sim Q$ is always true, so $P \wedge (Q \vee \sim Q)$ has the same truth value as $P$: T T F F.
$Q \wedge \sim Q$ is always false, so $(\sim P) \Rightarrow (Q \wedge \sim Q)$ is true exactly when $\sim P$ is false, that is, when $P$ is true: T T F F.
The columns agree, so the statements are logically equivalent.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses logical equivalence (Section 2.6).
